newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Foreigners can buy 10 pct of S1 Corp shrs.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners can buy 10 pct of S1 Corp shrs.

text.p: South Korea's Securities Supervisory Board said on Friday an additional 10 percent, or 229,920 shares, of S1 Corp's share capital would become available for foreign purchases from November 14.

Foreign investors are now unable to buy S1 Corp's shares in the market because the foreign stake in the company exceeded the 20 percent ceiling now being applied to most South Korean stocks, an official at the board said.
Japan's Secom Co has held a 25.67 percent stake in the security guard service company since it was set up in 1977 in a joint venture between Secom and Samsung Group.
South Korea limits foreigners to aggregate stakes of up to 20 percent for firms listed on the Seoul stock market.
But firms with foreign stakes exceeding the limit since their foundation may request exemptions from the board, the SSB official said.
